Mine has a manufacturing flaw where the handle on the valve to the lower tank does not completely clear the plastic of the unit when closing. It sits right up against the edge of the plastic, and if you move the thing around too much, or if it changes temperature substantially (e.g. in the trunk of a vehicle) then the handle gets pushed out a tiny bit. The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam If you like cold drinks, this is the ultimate coozie to get! They not only keep your drinks cold for hours, but they can actually make your drinks colder than they were from the refrigerator!

That is because each coozie has two main layers that work together to chill the drinks: an inner gel layer and a thick outer styrofoam layer.

When you put the coozie in the freezer, the gel layer freezes. This layer can actually drop the temperature of whatever drink you put int the coozie. It's like wrapping your drink in a blanket of ice! Then the styrofoam layer makes sure all that great coldness stays there. Drinks normally stay cold for several hours!

Another nice feature when using these coozies is that there is no problem with leaving wet rings on the furniture because the coozies prevent the normal condensation problem you have with cold drinks in a warm environment. I think this is because of the thick insulation layer. The cold inside is insulated from the warm outside which prevents condensation.

I know these coozies last for years. I originally found these coozies on MisterCold.com in 2006 and used them constantly ever since. I have taken them with me everywhere I go. They have held up very well for so much use. After 7 years of use, they finally began to show signs of wear (slight fraying at the bottom) so I decided it was time to get new ones. I was thrilled to find them here on Amazon! The new ones I got are just as good, if not better, than the original ones I bought years ago.

If you want to enjoy drinks that are cold, cold, cold and stay that way for hours, this is the perfect item for you. Just be sure to get a bunch because once your family and friends try them, they'll use them all the time. So you need plenty on hand to be sure there's always a cold one waiting for you! The rule in my house is you can use them as long as you don't take the last one. That way there's always at least one chilled and ready to go!
text_fidelity_b: The Fridge Drink Cooler - Lifoam

Kind of sucked that our full group of 5 could not enjoy the water together so on the final 2 days of our trip I took it into the ocean with us. The bag was never completely underwater. This morning I tried the sink test. Dropped some hats into the bag, filled up the kitchen sink, tossed the bag around a bit, and gave the bag a good squeeze. I could see air bubbles immediately. If air bubbles are coming out that means water is getting in. This bag is certainly getting returned. Now I'm wondering who should be responsible for my damaged electronics.

Aerobie Superdisc (6044022) My Black Lab can't get enough Frisbee, she demands it at least twice a day. Unlike the flying discs made specifically for dogs, these fly just like a real Frisbee (both in distance and flight pattern) yet have the soft rim so the dog"s mouth isn't injured when she catches it in mid-air. The brightly colored rim makes them easy to find when my throwing gets too wild and they end up somewhere she can't get to. The rim is squared off and ever so slightly raised above the actual disc which makes it easier for her to pick up if it lands flat on a slick or level surface.

I have tried many versions of Frisbees through the last 40 years of Labs in my life and these are by far the best. The one I just had to throw out was over 5 years old and eventually cracked in half but up until then flew perfectly despite being riddled with teeth marks, dents, and small cracks.

The size makes them unsuitable for small dogs (obviously) and because the rim is the only color they may be difficult for dogs (and humans) with imperfect eyesight to see.
text_fidelity_b: Aerobie Superdisc (6044022)

Citadel Black Zombie Apocalypse Survival Kit - Multi-Tool, Fire Starter, Keyring, Zombie Permit, Stickers, and More I am severely disappointed in this product. All the reviews make it out to be something it most certainly is not. This is just a novelty kit with about $5 work of product (if that). Neat concept, poor execution. If you're looking for a survival kit with products that will actually help you survive something in real life...THIS IS NOT IT. Even as a themed novelty kit, this is junk. Save your money.

The most useful items are the anti-bacterial goop and the bandaids.

The card multi-tool could be useful, but ALL the edges are sharp and can easily break skin.

The "tactical knife" is a card-knife that can neither be properly locked open or properly locked closed. It struggled with cutting the plastic this survival kit came wrapped in.

The dust mask is unfinished on the edges. It can easily become unraveled and had lots of loose ends fresh out of the package.

There was a tea candle. Yep.

Compass did not point North. Ever.

Glow sticks were not bright enough to illuminate the desk they were lying right on.

The fire starter is a joke. Don't get me wrong..With some skill it can be used, but it is absolute junk. I broke the metal bar after a few practice tries.

Overall, if I hadn't had a gift card to waste, I would have returned the item for a refund. Even my son who is all about zombie survival thought it was junk.
text_fidelity_b: Citadel Black Zombie Apocalypse Survival Kit - Multi-Tool, Fire Starter, Keyring, Zombie Permit, Stickers, and More

text_fidelity_a:
Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway This is a great way to store 12 sets of polyhedral dice for D&D and similar games. I'm not sure if you strictly-speaking need waterproof storage for that, but while the O-ring may be overkill, the locking clasps and overall durability are a cut above what you usually find on parts organizers. This is never, ever going to come open unexpectedly and spill its precious contents all over the place!

With the dividers installed as shown in my photo, 8 areas hold a set of 7 polyhedral dice perfectly. Five of those will also hold a set of 12 six-sided dice. The four larger areas hold somewhat more; I have 10 d20's in one of them comfortably.

The downside of this approach is that you're certainly not going to sneak up on anyone while carrying one of these full of plastic/resin dice. And if you're into metal dice, or the sort of gemstone dice where each of them costs more than this whole container, then this probably isn't how you want to store them. (But you could probably pad them properly with a bit more work.)

Color of the O-ring seems to vary. I have two black and one blue, but the Plano part number stamped into it is the same for all three.

If you are the sort of person who needs to compactly and securely transport a lot of dice, this is the best way I've found to do it.
text_fidelity_b: Plano 3640 Waterproof Stowaway

text_fidelity_a:
Kershaw 3140JB Wildcat Ridge w/Jigged Bone Inlay I bought this knife from another web site. The price was similar and it was a great deal. My first impression was "Wow! What a big knife"! My second impression was of the high quality that went into building this knife. Fit and finish are perfect. It was shaving sharp from the box. The brown leather sheath is of high quality and flawless.

In my city we are limited to knives with blades no longer than the width of our hands. This one squeaks by for me. I also have the Grant County, Black Gulch, Corral Creek all in clip point with jigged bone and the Corral Creek with the sheep's foot blade and ABS scales. Sure, they were all made in China and don't contain some highly exotic steel, but they work in the real world. And that's what matters to me.

I got a bad Black Gulch from a seller on Amazon and I am certain that it was a second because there were no info pamphlets and the knife was not in the usual plastic sleeve and it was dull as a brick. I gave it to a friend who is better at knife sharpening than I am. The Black Gulch that I got from 5 Starr was perfect. For me it just doesn't get much better than Kershaw and 5 Starr.

So, this is a large and beautiful knife for special occasions. No, I don't need knives as large as the Wildcat Ridge or Black Gulch for EDC, but if situation calls for it they are available. It is nice to know that I can carry a large knife without the Rambo tactical attitude that seems to be so popular now. It's a great knife at a great price.
text_fidelity_b: Kershaw 3140JB Wildcat Ridge w/Jigged Bone Inlay

Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps This was pretty easy to assemble, it appears very well made. Good wheels, straps and metal.

No matter how tight I make the two bands to the boat, they slide about a bit.

The wheels will tip to the right or left depending on how much the restraining bands shift.

I am using this trolley with an Old Town Pack Canoe. Those are bit shorter and wider in middle then many canoes. Thus it is easy for the bands to shift about, especially if you plan to pull the canoe with the wheels on the back end of the canoe. Were the move over pavement or other very smooth ground, it may go well. I have to move my canoe from back of yard over uneven ground and that causes the straps to shift on one side or the other.

When strap on on side slides back, the wheels won't run true and the canoe will be pulling in that direction. This will continue until you can't pull the canoe at all and have to reset the whole thing. For a long portage, this won't work.

The second time I used this thing, I put the trolley on the front and pushed it and things went better over a short distance. It was still balking and it was not a smooth run.

Next time I use it, I will try to set the trolley in the center of canoe and see how that goes. I expect some more experimentation will result in usable solution. But, if you have a fatter canoe with more of a narrowing at front and back, have to transport over uneven ground, and want to pull the canoe instead of pushing it; there may be things may not go well.
text_fidelity_b: Bonnlo Boat Kayak Canoe Cart Carrier Dolly Trailer Tote Trolley Transport Kayak Accessories Large with 20x2mm Aluminum Pipe Double Kickstands, Inflation Free Solid Tire Wheels, 2 Ratchet Straps

Contigo Superior 2.0 Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Handle and Leak-Proof Lid, Double-Wall Insulation Keeps Drinks Hot up to 7 Hours or Cold up to 18 Hours, 20oz Juniper When I order a product I am more interested in the negative reviews than the positive ones. What problems are other people having? Do the buyers understand how the product works or are they misusing it? Are there design errors in the product? Does it function as advertised? Is it possible that a string of bad reviews is due to a switch in manufacturers? That by the way is often the case and a company has to own that choice.

My first use resulted in an unintended torture test. After filling up the mug with my first cup of coffee in the morning -- when I am still a bit fumble fingered -- I dropped the full mug on our marble floor. You know that moment when the dropped item appears suspended in the air and you are anticipating a horrible crash and the resulting mess? Didn't happen here! Boy was I relieved. I hate to catch flak from my wife to start the day.

Since my wife will be using this mug on her commute to work I was most interested in the claim that it would keep liquids "hot for up to 7 hours". So I filled it up with hot coffee at 10:00 pm and opened it this morning at 7:00 am. For the mathematically challenged, which most of the younger kids seem to be these days, that is nine hours. When I popped the lid one-handed (which takes a bit of practice) and took a sip, I was rewarded with coffee that was better than warm but not quite hot.

Most users of course will not use this as a thermos to keep something hot or cold for 8-10 hours. Instead they will be steadily drinking/sipping from the cup until the beverage is finished. Constant repetitive opening and closing of the tab is bound to release heat faster and the remaining liquid will no doubt be at less than a desired temperature, but it was nice to see that it would function as promised.

So Contigo got it's act together, either by changing something in the product or finding a better manufacturer. The mug is a subtle pleasing color and fits perfectly in our vehicles. The lid opening mechanism comes stiff and takes a bit of use to work it loose. Even though the company says that you can put the lid (only) in the dishwasher, I always get better long-term results by hand washing them. Made in China.
text_fidelity_b: Contigo Superior 2.0 Stainless Steel Travel Mug with Handle and Leak-Proof Lid, Double-Wall Insulation Keeps Drinks Hot up to 7 Hours or Cold up to 18 Hours, 20oz Juniper

It has strong handles on the top of both sides with a single piece top. The inside measures 15 inches tall, 15 inches deep, and 32 inches wide. The top, while secured with plastic hinges, has a strap on the inside right end of the cooler to keep the top from over-opening and damaging the hinges. I think it's quite expensive for molded plastic, but it is made in the USA, so I'm giving it 5 stars.

M-Wave Bicycle Cycling Bag Since three vastly different items are in one listing: This is for the individual panniers. They seem solid enough. A bit of a loose seam or thread here or there, seen a lot worse. They have a good bit of space inside, I reckon 3 2-liter soda bottles a side with some stuff along the sides, but it'll be wonky because of the round bottom. The design of the top makes them water resistant, it's not a zipper. The stiffening material is thicker than I expected, will definitely provide protection and support for fairly heavy items. The clips and D-rings don't feel cheap or fragile.

The problems:

I ordered two and got two left-side panniers instead of a matched pair. I didn't even IMAGINE this would be a problem. Title, bullet points and description all need to say "left side only" if that's what it is, AND THE RIGHT SIDE OPTION NEEDS TO BE IN THE SAME LISTING. In any case I don't think heel striking will be a problem, they just look weird.

The top clips are sized for rails no more than 9mm(based on the diameter of the inner clearing, measured by caliper) while the side rails on an Ibera Touring Carrier Plus are 10.5mm. So it only clips on with the first clearing, not very strongly. They also come contracted shut- I had to stretch them out by putting 11.5mm thick pens in each one and leaving them overnight(see attached image.) Now I can at least get the clips on over the rail.

The next problem is that the Ibera rack has no good place to hook the stabilizing bungee. I will need to hook it somewhere weird, which means the panniers can't be taken off with one hand which is a disappointment.

I will try them a couple of times carrying groceries, the purpose I got them for. Their fate is up to how well they do the job.

text_fidelity_a:
Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker The Omron is quiet small and light. I can have it in a pocket along with my wallet or iPhone and I don't notice it's there. But I'm skeptical about its accuracy.

I took a few walks and compared the distance it recorded with the route mapped out as a walk in Google Maps. The Omron would typically under measure my distance anywhere from 30 to 60 percent. I re-checked the height, weight and stride settings but that had no effect. I guess it's unrealistic that a pedometer can accurately measure distance.

A more serious flaw is that the unit does not keep lifetime stats -- it's memory is only 7 days. If you have a workout schedule where you need to keep a log of your daily steps, the 7 day memory feature is quite nice for when you forget to write down a day's results, but I would think most people would like to know how many steps they've taken after a year.

While I suppose the distance issue is forgivable -- most people buy a pedometer to keep track of steps, not miles traveled -- the lack of lifetime memory makes it hard to recommend this unit.
text_fidelity_b: Omron HJ-203 Pedometer with Activity Tracker

text_fidelity_a:
Wilson X Connected Smart Basketball with Sensor That Tracks Shots To be honest, I wouldn't have ordered this if it weren't a complementary Vine item, but I'm glad I did. I never even heard of such a ball, let along did I think it would work--it works!

A friend of mine is a basketball coach, so I dropped by with this ball. After getting curious looks of disbelief and questions as to if I missed the deadline on April fools, we started trying it out. The players really responded to it. It felt like a normal ball (a good one at that), but they could immediately track their stats. That's the real genius here. Most of us can seen when the ball goes in the net or not, but keeping track of shots made/missed in practice can be tedious. Plus you can hook some speakers (preferably bluetooth) up and have this make solo practice a game and keep tabs. It really works!

Wow, this sounds amazing! It sure does, but there are some limitations. For now iPhone (or iOS) only (works on iOS 9 btw). Android is coming. It also isn't for tracking layups or dunks, rather it's designed for 7+ foot shots. It's also not perfect. I was hoping for 95%+ accuracy, but 85-90% accuracy (requires a net to work at all btw). That's still amazing, but there's room for improvement. Also it's more useful in solo practice, as there are plenty of other ways to make group practice interesting. That's not to say it's not useful there, but $200 can probably be better used in that context.

As a solo practice tool, this is awesome. Like a fitbit or other modern doodad, this aids in accountability and adds a game like aspect to a mundane activity. Sure great players have always driven themselves to taking thousands of shots a day, but not everyone has that focus. This can definitely help, and while the accuracy is still a work in progress, over thousands of shots, it will show trends (and hopefully improvement). Plus it talks to social media, so if by chance you and a buddy have one, you can share stats and trash talk on Facebook. Isn't life grand! On a more serious note, it can show coach, dad (or mom), that you're using it and getting your reps in, to help justify that expensive summer basketball camp.

So is this a gadget for early adapters and hard core basketball players? Mostly. We all have different budgets, and for some $200 isn't much, but for many it is, and yeah, it's a niche. It'll do more to help your game than a pair of fancy shoes or expensive athletic wear, and for the gym rats who put in hours a day working on shooting, this is a great (and novel) addition to the arsenal. For everyone else, maybe wait a bit.

5 stars if you're in the niche
text_fidelity_b: Wilson X Connected Smart Basketball with Sensor That Tracks Shots

text_fidelity_a:
Atpylan Large Capacity Lunch Bag for Women Men, Reusable Cooler Bag Collapsible Coolers for Travel I call this a tote rather than a cooler because it does more than a cooler does. In fact, I'll be using it mostly to transport warm items than I will cold.

PROs
- I love the dark blue color(C2-blue). I saw a photo on a different review and it looked like a brighter blue. Unless there was a different color offered that I'm unaware of, the dark blue is true to color on the listing.
- This will hold quite a bit. If you're like me and plan on using it to bring food items to potlucks, this will do well.
- The top pocket (also insulated) can hold any utensils, spices, napkins, or other items you may want to bring along. Or more ice packs, if using it as a cooler.
- There's an additional front (insulated) pocket and two side mesh pockets for whatever your heart desires. Pockets galore.
- It's collapsible.
- There are two handles that meet in the center and can be held together with a short hook and loop sleeve. That makes it so convenient, particularly if you're carrying heavier items. The handles aren't digging into your hands then. Instead there's a sleeve adding comfort.
- There is an optional shoulder strap, however, see the cons below for further detail...

CONs
- The optional shoulder strap is nice to have, however, the point of weight bearing lies upon two plastic hooks on each side. I've included a photo of one of them. I don't believe I would trust those when carrying heavier loads.
- The bottom of the bag does not have a hard surface. I will likely find something I can put on the bottom to make it firm when carrying items of different sizes, etc. Perhaps I'll double up on some cardboard and wrap it in foil or something. I'm not sure yet.

All in all I love this bag and would definitely recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Atpylan Large Capacity Lunch Bag for Women Men, Reusable Cooler Bag Collapsible Coolers for Travel

text_fidelity_a:
OUUKER Full Face Snorkel Mask, Anti-Fog Anti-Leak Snorkeling Mask UV Protection Diving Snorkel Mask with Detachable Camera Mount for Adults and Youths We’ve seen this type of mask - similar - so thought we’d give it a try. Yea, it looks cool and with our backgrounds in snorkeling and Scuba we thought this might be fun for a larger view. I had noted another review saying the view was distorted, but not everyone is comfortable looking through masks, so perhaps that was the case.

First, it fit me fine, but my wife not as well. I have a larger, rounder head, hers is smaller, more narrow. This version she was unable to reduce it down enough. She was never comfortable enough and it did leak for her. I was able to use it without a leak. It fit my head fine and out of the water I was very comfortable.

There was a moment when I first went under I had to think about a different kind of breathing from normal Scuba or snorkeling. Once I was past that, breathing was fine. I felt completely comfortable breathing within the mask and not worried about how the system is set up.

The other reviewer was correct - it wasn’t just a different person’s experience - but the view is distorted. In a very large range of view right to left, up and down, if you look straight ahead things directly out front are clear, but as you move outwards, even just a bit, the distortion begins and continues. One must actually turn the head in order to keep the view clear and undistorted. In other words, a fish right in front of you will look fine, but anything even a few inches to either side will begin to look distorted - for some it might even cause discomfort.

We tested this in a swimming pool - controlled environment - so I was able to swim around and not feel nauseous with the distortion (no tide, waves, reefs, or other things to disorient and bounce one’s view off), but could easily see if I were in the ocean/Gulf that might be different. It is possible someone else might be fine. However, I would add that my wife, before she became too uncomfortable with the leaking, also felt and saw the distortion.

The other thing that made this uncomfortable for me was the buoyancy - this literally held me at the surface. I had to push my head down in order to go even an inch or two deeper, and that was an effort after awhile. My wife noticed the effort I was having to out in and felt it herself. This also lent itself to a pressure within the mask - any time I’d get my face to a certain depth I could feel the pressure build and push the mask even tighter/harder against my face and head. This became uncomfortable in and of itself.

I’d like to be able to recommend this mask - it is a great idea, especially for someone not sure about snorkeling/breathing with a mask. But this version just does not deliver. I cannot in all good consciousness recommend this mask.
text_fidelity_b: OUUKER Full Face Snorkel Mask, Anti-Fog Anti-Leak Snorkeling Mask UV Protection Diving Snorkel Mask with Detachable Camera Mount for Adults and Youths

text_fidelity_a:
Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper This is made of a light, soft, flame retardant flannel.

It has a long white zipper which goes almost to the toes, with an easy snap at the top.

The fabric is cute with Patriots logo.

It has white stitching for accent.

It is 100% polyester. I prefer cotton which breathes better.

It has two pesky labels at the top back.

You are supposed to turn this inside out when you wash on cold, gentle cycle with like colors. Do not use fabric softener or it will impact flame retardant ability. Non-chlorine bleach. Tumble dry low.

It was made in Bangladesh.

Suggestions for improvement: use more cotton in fabric, substitute print for labels at upper back, and perhaps skip the flame retardant chemicals. 3.5 stars

Here's some info which discourages flame retardant fabrics close to children's skin:
A study published in August 2014 found that PBDEs (polybrominated diphenyl ethers), the most commonly used fire-retardant chemicals, were linked to numerous health problems.

Researchers found the chemicals were to blame for:

thyroid disruption
early onset of puberty
cognitive problems
delayed mental and physical development
“The chemicals used to make pajamas and other consumer products flame-retardant show up in water, wildlife, and human breast milk,” says pediatrician Michael Macknin, MD.

According to Dr. Macknin, the chemicals in fire retardants do diminish the flammability of products treated with them and have been associated with decreased burn injuries in children. However, the chemicals aren’t well-bound to the fabric fibers at times and can leech out. This allows the fire-retardant chemicals to float free in the environment.

“The long-term impact these chemicals may have on health and cognition is not closely scrutinized,” says Dr. Macknin. “They are often put on the market without long-term studies of their safety.”

Other dangers besides pajamas
These chemicals are found in furniture and mattresses as well as cell phones, television remotes and numerous other consumer plastics, says Dr. Macknin.

“If the tag on a sofa or mattress you’re planning to buy says, ‘this article complies with flammability requirements of California Bureau of Home Furnishings Technical Bulletin 117’, or language to that effect, it likely contains pounds of PBDEs,” he says.

You’ll find this sort of notice on numerous children’s products like car seats, strollers, toys and changing mats. According to Dr. Macknin and other health experts, these added chemicals may put your child at a greater risk than the flames they claim to inhibit. An alternative to chemically treated flame-retardant pajamas are close-fitting pajamas made of natural fibers. Some fabrics meet smolder standards without added chemicals.
text_fidelity_b: Outerstuff Toddler NFL Piped Raglan Full-Zip Jumper

text_fidelity_a:
sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors This review is for the sixthreezero EVRYjourney Women's Step-Through 500-Watt Electric Bike

The short version is: This is a great bike, sixthreezero has great support, and I highly recommend the bike and company.

My mom has some back issues, including fused vertebrae, and over the years, the number of physical activities she's able to participate in has declined. Long family bike rides on a normal bike were no longer an option. For that reason, in February we decided to go to a local Pedego store and rent e-bikes for my mom and wife. We did a 15 mile ride, and everyone, including my mom and wife, loved it.

My mom liked it so much that she reconfirmed the prices when we got back, but it was definitely outside of her budget.

We both spent the next several months looking for an e-bike deal that was too good to say no to. There's some cheap options online, a Costco mountain e-bike, some nice bikes that are out of our budget, both online and locally, but nothing that was amazing...

Until Prime Day 2019.

sixthreezero's 250-watt bikes were on sale during Prime Day. I don't even see them available now, but it was a great deal, and I did some research before phoning my mom and telling her I think we'd found the deal she was looking for. After telling my mom about it, she ordered one, then asked if I was getting one for my wife. I was on the fence, because it's still a lot of money, until she said, "Don't think about how much you're spending per ride. Do you want to have lots of happy memories of the family riding together or are you OK without those?"

Well said, Mom. I ordered one the next day.

Now, I don't see the 250-watt bikes on Amazon anymore, but when they were here, the online documentation, both here and over at sixthreezero at the time we ordered made the basic functionality seem the same between the 250-watt and the 500-watt bicycles. The key feature both my mom and wife were looking for was the ability to pedal with adjustable resistance, but leverage the throttle with the left thumb to accelerate with the motor when needed to either catch up quickly or tackle hills without issue. (And without changing the level of pedal assistance.)

Some of our first impressions were not great. My mom's bike showed up looking amazing, and my dad assembled it without issue, but the throttle did not behave as expected. (The boost was limited to the level of pedal assist you were in.) My wife's bike showed up, but the fender and rack were both badly bent.

Before buying the bike, I saw that sixthreezero, if you bought directly from them, was willing to offer 365 day test drives, and seemed really focused on customer satisfaction. The Amazon reviews seemed positive, and the box the bike came in offered free assembly at a local bike store. (I'm not sure how that works because I've built over a dozen bikes and this bike is easy to assemble.) That said, I had a damaged bike and it didn't perform as I was expecting. I was definitely concerned when I reached out to sixthreezero.

After multiple calls, photos and a video to confirm that my 250-watt bike did not perform the way their 500-watt did (the technician I was working with only had a 500-watt readily available to troubleshoot with), they were willing to work with my mom and I to find a satisfactory proposal that would allow us to send back the 250-watt bikes and they would ship us 500-watt versions.

They were polite and reasonable throughout the process, but I was still nervous about bike number two, since the first bike did arrive with issues outside of the e-bike functionality. I was pleasantly surprised that they seem to have people working there who seem to genuinely want to make sure their customers love their bikes.

The 500-watt bike went together very easily, and after assembling and tuning the bike, I took it for a ride. The bike was a blast.

The only thing that jumped out at me as being substantially different from the Pedego my wife rode was the seat post. The Pedego had a shock in the seat post, which doesn't do a lot, but is better than nothing. I ordered a "Sunlite Pillar Suspension Seat Post, 27.2 x 350mm, Silver" from Amazon, which seemed like a good improvement to the bike, which is otherwise fantastic. (The rigid seat post makes the ride a tad rough, which is why I gave comfort 4 stars, I'd bump that to 5 with the suspension seat post.)

My wife says she finds the sixthreezero 500-watt basically the same as the Pedego. I'm sure there are differences, but the only big one we see is the price.

I can't adequately describe an e-bike in words alone, but if you have the option to rent one locally, I highly suggest you try it. It's a lot of fun. I'm not a fan of skilled cyclists tearing up mountain bike trails with heavier, faster e-bikes, nor would I advocate road bikers throw electric motors on their bikes, but the joy e-bikes are able to bring families by leveling the field for families that want to ride together is awesome. And sixthreezero's EVRYjourney cruiser is a fantastic bike for those people.

We're averaging speeds of more than half a mile per hour more as a family than we used to, and my wife comes home with a smile on her face while my kids come home having used up more energy and me having gotten a better work out. I know this bike is not cheap, but I like the way my mom put it to me:

Would you rather be out riding with your loved ones? This is a fantastic option for those who can't match the speed or stamina of the people they're riding with.
text_fidelity_b: sixthreezero Electric-Bicycles Around The Block Women's Ebike, 250/500 Watt Motor, 7-Speed Beach Cruiser Bicycle with Rear Rack, 26" Wheels, Multiple Colors

text_fidelity_a: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color This style of stringer is really the best kind to use if you want to keep your fish alive and well while you are fishing. The nylon versions pile the fish on top of each other, and it literally suffocates them and you end up with a lot of dead fish to clean. (if anyone reading this knows anything about fishing and actually eats the fish they catch like I do....they know that this is kind of a bad thing. makes the meat taste all funky) with this stringer, you can easily pierce the lower lip of the fish (do NOT put it through their gills as this will kill them quicker than anything! just a little tip for those who may not have known this) it will keep them alive pretty much until the time you clean them depending on where and how you transport them to the cleaning station. But essentially it's a good all around stringer that will serve you well if used properly. they DO tend to rust if you let the water dry on them over time especially if used in salt water conditions, but they are pretty inexpensive over all so easy to replace as needed. I will often use this in unison with the nylon stringers to kind of extend the stringer a bit for when I am fishing from the shore as it gives the fish more room to swim around and stay active. but it is a good one for clipping to the side of the kayak or canoe. just don't use it on a motor boat. (Get a livewell or a cooler for that, because speeding through the water on a stringer will actually drowned the fish believe it or not.....yes you can drowned a fish. lol) anyway, hope this helps any beginner anglers out there.
text_fidelity_b: Eagle Claw 04300-005 Invincible Chain Stringer, 46-Inch, 9-Snap,Multi-Color

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 2 Heart Rate + Fitness Wristband, Teal, Small (US Version) My first Charge 2 was wonderful until it stopped reading my HR correctly after 5 months. My Charge 2 would tell me that my HR was 130+ when I was sitting or not even wearing it. On top of that, the wristband broke around the same time. I contacted support and they tried to fix the problem by having me restart my Fitbit however it did not work. Customer support was nice enough to offer me a replacement after going back and forth a few times.

Unfortunately the replacement Fitbit sent me was defective. I put the Fitbit on and tighten the wristband and position the Fitbit to the correct spot on my wrist but the Fitbit would not pickup my HR. After a few hours it started to read my HR however the reading was completely off. I took the Fitbit off and it continued to give me an outrageously high HR. It said my HR was 150 when I was just sitting or not wearing it. That's riduculous! I tried resetting the Fitbit many times but it did not solve the problem. I ended up wearing the Fitbit for a few months to see if it was just a one time fluke (I was also too lazy and feeling too frustrated to contact customer support AGAIN). Unfortunately the Charge 2 continued to read my heart rate incorrectly. To add onto the problem, this new Fitbit would think I'm walking when I'm just driving. I understand that most Fitbit will do this sometimes but mines was doing it all the time! No way I walked closed to 10000 steps each day. I've been lazy as F and I've been doing a lot of sitting these past few months LOL.

I finally found some free time today and hollered at customer service. They asked me to reset my Fitbit, so I did, but as I was doing so, my Fitbit battery suddenly drained and my Fitbit died. WHAT? After waiting for my Fitbit to come back to life the rep asked me to fire up the app and sync my Fitbit to the app. We tried 5 times and even reset the app but it didn't work. UGH this is now the FOUTH issue I'm having with this Charge 2. What a nightmare.

The rep quickly offered me a 50% discount for a new device or get my Fitbit Charge 2 replaced. NO WAY was I willing to get a THIRD Charge 2 and risk having to go through the headache of contacting customer service again if my THIRD Fitbit turns out to be defective too. I pestered the rep to see if she could give me a better discount, refund me, or give me credit to upgrade to a better model. Sadly, the rep and the supervisor did not have the power to offer me a better deal.

*When I asked for a refund or credit for a better model, the rep responded with this:

"I really understand your frustration Kimberly, however please be assured that our product team is constantly working to ensure that our products go through rigorous testing so that they can last and endure as expected."

LIES! Obviously Fitbit doesn't tell well enough if I've received two defective Charge 2.

*I asked if my warranty will be extended if I obtain a THIRD Charge 2:

Rep - If the device is out of warranty we will be unable to replace it and we may offer a discount to purchase a new device.
Rep - I understand your concern Kimberly, but if you decide to use the 50% discount to make a upgrade the new device will have a new warranty.
Rep - When you receive a replacement device, the replacement device has 30 days of warranty or the remaining of the original warranty.
Rep - So if the device fails which is not something that we expect to happen you have 30 days from the moment that the device is received in order to contact us again and get a replacement if necessary.

Sigh, this offer is not good enough. I wonder if I can sue for giving me a headache if my THIRD Fitbit also turns out to be defective...

*I then inquired about what happens if I have to claim a FOURTH Fitbit?

Me: would I qualify for a different model at that point
Me: or just another 50 % off discount

Me: Well that's not good

Me: how Do I guarantee that I get a NEW one
Rep: Since that depends on the warehouse Kimberly we have no control about if a new or factory-certified refurbished device will be sent.

I really wished Fitbit had a better buyer protection plan for unfortunate people like me. If you're reading this Fitbit, I would really like my money back or an upgrade to the Blaze or Ionic.

text_fidelity_a:
REDESS 11 Pack Exercise Resistance Bands with Handles Exercise Stretch Fitness Home Set Include 5 Stackable Exercise Bands with Carry Bag, Handles, Legs Ankle Straps & Door Anchor FINAL UPDATE - I ordered a Fitfort set, which has the same function as this package but doesn't seem destined to fail. I donated this set to Salvation Army the day Fitfort arrived. End of story.

UPDATE - After 4 months, the nylon bands on one handle failed. I'm improvising with rope earlier, the attachment to one band had to be fixed, and the black band has now torn. Was this worth four months' gym membership?

After one use, I find this adequate. I find good all-around routines, inlcuding one for straps, on darebee.

This kit provides a lot more resistance than the latex straps I'd been using. And the concept of being able to adjust your resistance by combining the five bands is good in principle. It's clear this will work better if you have good technique—slow, smooth movements, not jerky Yanks. But the small problems add up:

The concept is cool, but not unique. Post-COVID, there are a lot of these packs available, many for $10-15 less. Consider them!

Many reviews cite the handles as a weak point, and it's clear they will fail in time. They lasted fine through the first workout. (See below.)

These bands give different levels of resistance, but I'm not sure how much. There are 2 contradictory weight schemes in the Amazon posting (diff weights, diff color). Hint: blue is stronger than green. Also, I have no confidence that the numerical values are right. Is black really 40/50 pounds? Either I'm really strong...

Reviewers also reported snapped bands, and maybe it might be good to warm them up with a stretch before your workout. I believe the black and blue will snap if I stretch from from the floor to overhead, no I will have to kneel for military presses. And move smoothly thru your exercises, don't jerk or yank. It's better form, and will avoid snapping.

The Velcro ankle straps? Ha! Loop them through and they are secure!

UPDATE after 3 months: this set works, but it's not durable. One of the handles will tear, and then I'll have to re-sew it. The black band came loose from one of its hooks, and I re-fit it. The convenient carrying sack is fraying, like the ankle bands. This has been a lifeline during the lockdown that made my gym unsafe, but this is not a long-term fitness tool. It just won't last.

(CAUTION - the high rating for this set is because the reviews are mixed with what must be a very good beanie. Users of this set average 1-2 stars.)

Magicmode Carbon Badminton Racket Set-with 6 Shuttlecocks and 1 Bag We have enjoyed playing badminton in a club setting, but due to Covid, have been unable to get back. So we decided to get a set for ourselves at home - as well as a net - and still be able to play. This set includes: a bag, 2 rackets, and container of 6 shuttlecocks. I would call this a set ideal for families, the backyard, beach, or picnics, but not for someone at the intermediate or advanced play/club play.

This is a great set. We got two nets here on Amazon for different settings, and took this set to our community tennis court.

The Bag: This is a great bag for this set. It allows one to carry both rackets and the tube of included shuttlecocks. That said, it would be a little better if the bag were even an inch longer. These are a tight fit at the current size. Even without the tube, these rackets have to be in essence pushed in in order to fit. But overall it's a great bag, looks great, and makes carrying easy.

The Rackets: These are nice. Again, this price point, these rackets are for family or couples looking for an hour of fun in the backyard, picnic, or on the beach - not a club setting. They have that nice sound when they connect, and they have a great distance on them. Lightweight, there was no fatigue after an hours play.

The Shuttlecocks: This is a great tube - 6 included. They are feathers, so nicer than the plastic kind. They get a nice sail to them. As feather, these will be damaged quickly, but one can continue to play for a good amount of time. We used one for a few games before needing to trade out. Plastic ones, once damaged, tend to need to be changed more quickly - in my experience.

This is a great set and for the right setting and players, perfect. We are happy and happy to recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako Got this to mount a MiNewt 150 on my helmet, and it's working well so far. It's kind of a tie-down thing with some pipe-insulation-like rubber under the plastic foot/pedestal to keep it from sliding around on the helmet. I've had it for about 2-3 weeks, so I can't comment on durability, but it has the same quick-release setup as the handlebar mount packaged with the 150. It tilts front and back, though not side-to-side. I'm using it with a Bell road helmet, and had no problems mounting it right in the center--as long as you have symmetrical vents in your helmet, you should be ok.

Good Stuff
With the right adjustments, you can get a good view of what's (well) ahead of you, and having it helmet-mounted allows you to pan and sweep the road ahead for pointy stuff and potholes. I also use it to alert drivers when approaching intersections--a quick look left and right gives a flash in their direction to get attention. The on-helmet setup seems to allow for longer "reach" from the light as well. One added bonus--drivers of high-profile vehicles (monster trucks, etc.) are more likely to see you since the light is well above the handlebars.

Notes and Concerns
If going for long rides in the dark, I'd recommend keeping a small blinky on the handlebars to complement the helmet mount (if you're not looking straight-ahead, your light isn't either). The mount is also made mainly of plastic--not sure what that does for long-term durability--may want to take it off if not doing night/dark rides, to minimize UV damage in the sun, etc. The mount does make the light sit rather high on the head, so it's not going to improve your aerodynamics or get you any style points (like a Roman centurion helmet profile), and it of course adds a bit of weight to the helmet.

Overall
I'd recommend this, especially for anyone who rides in the dark frequently or for long periods of time.
text_fidelity_b: NiteRider Commuter Helmet Mount F/Cordless & Mako

text_fidelity_a:
Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve CONTEXT:
After watching a documentary about teflon and plastic etcetera, and learning that all similar products leech into the water, I opted to start using glass. After using a Hydro, I was a little bit bummed that my water wouldn't be cold AF for hours on end, but I figured it was worth the sacrifice. I have smaller glass bottles, but with as much as I workout, I needed a way to track and increase my intake. I found this one and immediately needed it because of its size!

PROS:
- The neoprene sleeve it comes with actually does a pretty good job of keeping the water cold AND helps with keeping the condensation at bay. It never gets soaking wet.
- It holds so much water! One bottle of this a day is one 1.4 liters.
- Water just tastes so much better. I don't care what anyone says... water tastes better out of glass.
- The handle addition on the neoprene is a huge plus! It helps with lugging this thing around.

CONS:
- This isn't really a con for me, BUT I know it will be for others. The water doesn't stay cold for hours... I live in Hawaiʻi, so naturally, it gets warm pretty quick (but keep reading for tips). If you live somewhere cold, like Washington, I don't think you'll really have a problem. :)
- Obviously, this bottle is pretty freakin large. So carrying it around can be a b-word.

TIPS:
- I learned that putting ice in my bottle helps a lot with keeping it cold throughout the day (not even kidding). I usually fill the bottle with 1/4 ice and the rest with filtered water. By the time I am getting to the bottom of my bottle, the ice has melted, but the water is still cold.

OVERALL:
I can't recommend this bottle enough. It is perfect for me!
text_fidelity_b: Ferexer 48 oz Sports Borosilicate Glass Water Bottle with Bamboo Lid with Neoprene Sleeve

text_fidelity_a:
Cola Bottle Vacuum Insulated Double Wall Stainless Steel Leak-proof Cola Shape Sports Water Bottle Keeps Your Drink Hot & Cold 17oz(500ml) The Skyline 17 oz premium insulated stainless steel bottle is a great choice! I own several S'Well bottles that look and function identical to this one at a MUCH lower price. A co-worker really liked my S'Well bottle but as previously stated, S'Well bottles are $25+ a bottle and that's more than I wanted to spend on a gift, so I was looking for a comparable alternative and I found it with the FLY Skyline. I wanted to make sure the Fly Skyline would keep water ice cold all day, I filled the Skyline bottle with ice cold water the before work and the bottle was effective at keeping the water ice cold the next day. The bottle is constructed of high quality stainless steel and looks/feels like it will last forever. The bottle holds 17 ounces of liquid, which is perfect for taking to work to be able to drink ice cold water at your desk. The lip on the bottle provides a very comfortable surface to drink from. The bottle includes a screw on lid that provides a leak-proof seal eliminating the worry and fear that the liquid will spill out of the bottle. The bottle states that it can keep beverages hot for 12 hours and cold for 24; I have only used the bottle for keeping beverages cold so I can only confirm that it can keep beverages cold for 24 hours (not sure about effectiveness of ability to keep beverages hot as I have not tried). The opening will easily accommodate "half moon" shaped ice but you will struggle to place ice cubes in the opening. Overall I was very satisfied with this bottle so if you are looking for a bottle that will keep your beverage hot/cold all day the Skyline stainless steel coke bottle is a great choice!

Pros:
-Keeps water cold/hot for a long time
-Stainless steel construction will last forever
-Screw top provides leak-proof seal
-Great textured surface makes holding onto bottle easy and slip free

I was fortunate enough to have received this product at a discount for my honest and unbiased opinion. I would definitely purchase this bottle again.
text_fidelity_b: Cola Bottle Vacuum Insulated Double Wall Stainless Steel Leak-proof Cola Shape Sports Water Bottle Keeps Your Drink Hot & Cold 17oz(500ml)

Aegend Swim Goggles, 2 Pack Swimming Goggles No Leaking Adult Men Women Youth I’ve been pool swimming a few years now and I do wear glasses now since I’m over middle-aged.

I bought both the rounded goggles and flat lens goggles from these guys after reading an avid swimmers review speaking about only wearing flat lens. They’re the funky ones pro swimmers wear. Now I know why.

What a difference! I will never ever ever wear non-flatlands goggles again. I guarantee if you try each on, you will wonder why they even make curved lens goggles!

Goggles are made of a substance that does not lend itself to being curved. Every single thing is blurred. Above or below water. You put a flat lens pair on and boom! Every single thing is clear above and below water.

It’s such a pleasure. It’s like wiping grease away from a window and seeing clearly again. I thought I’d have issues with being near sighted… But of course water magnifies and with flat lenses, nothing was an issue.

All thanks to reading one of many reviews when trying to get to the bottom of what swim goggles on Amazon are great.

(In my pics the flat lens are the lighter lens ones reflecting my window better)

Action 10X1 180Mm Solid Track Rear Hub Axle Set I got tired of the rear tire shifting around on my heavily modified SE Stout 29er with the Deore XT FH-M756 Disc Hub in QR. I had to get this with to stop it from happening. The QR wasn't holding on during excessive/extreme braking.

This product is a life saver!

What I did was just use the track nuts and the axle, I had to re-use the bearing races because they were designed specifically for the Deore hub. I flushed out the old lube and used Moly red lithium with a Timken OK load index of 55. I also installed new BC Precision bearings. I tightened everything up and had it on my bike in less than an hour. These track nuts hold on like there is no tomorrow!

I feel so much more confident going down black diamonds now that I don't have to worry about my rear wheel shifting around.
